abstract_sentences.text: While on-policy distillation offers dense supervision for training small reasoning models, its optimization dynamics in the multimodal domain remain under-explored.

In this work, we challenge the standard monolithic view of Vision-Language Model (VLM) distillation by mathematically decomposing the loss into two distinct components: the language prior and visual grounding.

evidence.anchor: decomposing the loss into two components

abstract_sentences.text: Our analysis uncovers that gradient vectors for these components are nearly orthogonal, indicating that the objective of aligning with the teacher’s language distribution is geometrically independent from the objective of matching its visual perception.
Consequently, standard optimization passively follows a suboptimal compromise trajectory that implicitly balances the two objectives.

Hypothesizing that visual grounding constitutes the primary bottleneck for vision-language reasoning, we introduce Visual Gradient Steering (VGS), a method that dynamically reorients the update vector to prioritize the visual subspace.

Experimental results on multiple distillation settings and complex multimodal benchmarks demonstrate that VGS significantly outperforms the standard monolithic formulation of on-policy distillation, achieving superior grounding with minimal training overhead.

evidence.anchor: superior grounding with minimal training overhead

claim_closure.claim: Language-prior and visual-grounding gradients create a tension that makes standard monolithic OPD a compromise direction.
claim_closure.method_response: Bayes decomposition, q*T construction, and VDS define the two components and diagnostic.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 3 gives VDS-bin angles, including about 92 degrees at bin 9 and an about 42-degree standard-to-visual offset.

evidence.anchor: orthogonality between language and vision gradients
gradient acts as a passive bisector

claim_closure.claim: VGS can prioritize visual grounding without degrading linguistic fluency.
claim_closure.method_response: Equations 13–18 add visual steering and selective Language Preservation on top 30% VDS tokens.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 4 shows LLang divergence without LP and a lower final VGS-LP curve.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 11 says VGS explicitly prioritizes the visual subspace.

claim_closure.claim: VGS outperforms standard monolithic OPD on complex multimodal reasoning benchmarks.
claim_closure.method_response: VGS-LP is evaluated with a shared GRPO teacher at 2B and 4B student scales.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 reports +2.37 average Acc@1 for 2B and +1.56 for 4B, with negative individual cells also retained.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 11 repeats that VGS outperforms standard distillation.

evidence.anchor: significantly outperforms the standard monolithic formulation

claim_closure.claim: VGS serves as a useful regularizer for GRPO fine-tuning.
claim_closure.method_response: Equation 22 combines GRPO surrogate reward and VGS-LP with alpha.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 2 reports a +1.79 average Acc@1 difference versus GRPO plus Standard-KD for a 2B student.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 11 calls VGS a critical regularizer for RL fine-tuning.

claim_closure.claim: VGS gains occur where visual grounding is a primary bottleneck without compromising text-only reasoning.
claim_closure.method_response: VDS supplies the conceptual grouping mechanism; steering alters the visual term.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 10 shows high-visual ordering and reported uniform low-visual/text-only performance.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 11 does not separately quantify this scope claim.

claim_closure.claim: Adaptive token-level VGS can modestly improve over fixed VGS.
claim_closure.method_response: Equations 24–25 assign three steering levels by VDS thresholds.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 5 reports 46.53 Adaptive-VGS average versus 46.10 fixed VGS for 2B.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 11 does not reclaim the adaptive variant.

final_judgment.single_storyline: The paper reframes VLM on-policy distillation as a language-prior versus visual-grounding gradient-direction problem, then uses VGS plus LP to favor the visual term [PDF p. 3–6, Sections 3–4].
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the decomposition, Eq. 1–22, Figures 2–6, Tables 1–2, two student scales, and the GRPO extension [PDF p. 2–9].
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A–G move scaling evidence, implementation, prompt, sensitivity, cost, dependency scope, adaptive VGS, qualitative examples, and explicit limitations to pages 13–24 [PDF p. 13–24].
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2 pipeline, Figure 3 diagnostic, Figure 4 intervention consequence, and Table 1 benchmark result form a compact mechanism–intervention–outcome sequence [PDF p. 2, 4–6].
final_judgment.largest_gap: The strongest benchmark and grounding claims lack seed counts, repeat counts, benchmark denominators, broad uncertainty reporting, and a qualitative-example selection protocol [PDF p. 4, 6–8, 18].
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a decomposed joint objective, show the decomposition, a measurable diagnostic, a directional intervention, a reverse or component control, and outcome evidence that uses the same unit of analysis.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This pattern needs identifiable sub-objectives and a diagnostic linked to task success; if a teacher has no distinguishable visual response, the visual gradient is approximately zero and VGS reduces to standard distillation [PDF p. 18, Appendix G].

document_layout.description: Main prose is two-column. Figure 1 shares page 1 with the abstract and introduction; Figures 2–4 and 6 and Tables 1–2 are full width, while Figure 5 occupies the right column. Appendix F uses full-page qualitative cards.

statistics_notes.aggregation: Table 1 and Table 2 report a row per benchmark and an Average across seven benchmarks; the within-benchmark denominator and weighting are not stated.
statistics_notes.uncertainty: Figure 3 labels mean plus or minus 0.5 STD. The paper does not give a seed count, confidence interval, p-value, hypothesis test, bootstrap, regression, or multiple-comparison procedure.

lexical_rhetoric.method: Lowercase rough count over pages 1–9 after removing references, table values, formula fragments, and figure/table captions; counts are descriptive and susceptible to PDF hyphenation.
lexical_rhetoric.strong_vs_hedged_context: Strong terms include significantly 5, superior 4, outperforms 4, consistently 4, and critical 4; cautious terms include typically 4, minimal 4, hypothesize 1, suggests 1, arguably 1, and likely 1. This is rhetorical location, not linguistic inference.
